correctness.rationale: For the specified four-dimensional two-vertex exponential-comparison logistic Keller–Segel ODE, the (M,z,C,w) change gives exact equations and isolates eigenvalue -β. At a positive unequal equilibrium, t=z/M∈(0,t_max), M=K/(1+t²), z=Kt/(1+t²), w=αz/δ. The scalar equilibrium branch χ=δX(t)/(αK), X=(1+t²)atanh(h)/t with h=t[1+κ(1-t²)/(1+t²)], is strictly increasing because h=(t+v)/(1+tv) and both atanh(s)/s and relevant positive factors increase; its limit 1+κ supplies the threshold. The reduced 3×3 Jacobian J=[[-a,-b,0],[d,-e,F],[0,α,-δ]] has q=αF/δ=e(1-h²)atanh(h)/h with 0<q<e. The exact identity D=ae+bd-aq=-(rη/2)G_t>0 follows from branch derivative G_t<0. The cubic coefficients A=a+e+δ, B=T+δ(a+e-q), C0=δD and AB-C0=(a+e)T+δ(a+e+δ)(a+e-q)+δaq are all strictly positive, completing Routh–Hurwitz and hyperbolic attraction, independent of d sign. Independently symbolically checked D+(rη/2)G_t=0 and numerically evaluated five distinct positive-rate admissible equilibria (κ=0.2,0.5,1,2,4), all with negative real eigenvalues and strictly positive Hurwitz margins. Boundary χ=χ_c, zero rates and global basins not covered.

value.rationale: For a natural two-patch finite metapopulation chemotaxis model, a complete all-positive-parameter stability certificate for both patterned branches rules out secondary local Hopf, steady-state, or other spectral destabilization as chemotactic sensitivity grows. Existence and monotonicity of equilibria alone cannot settle these stability questions; the strict cubic Hurwitz factorization supplies a nontrivial missing dynamical classification.

limitations: At strictly positive rates and χ>χ_c, both positive nonuniform equilibria are locally exponentially attracting; no global convergence, threshold-point hyperbolicity, or general graph extension.
